strings: Following the disastrous fall of Gnomeregan to troggs and radiation, displaced gnomes have fled into the snowy wilds of Dun Morogh. Outside Anvilmar, an engineer named Felix Whindlebolt lost his vital belongings and tools to Frostmane troll scavengers during the panicked evacuation.

When subterranean troggs overran the high-tech city of Gnomeregan, High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and his advisors authorized the release of radioactive gas in a desperate bid to eradicate the invaders. The gambit backfired catastrophically, slaying thousands of innocents, mutating survivors into mindless leper gnomes, and forcing the remaining populace into a frantic exodus across Dun Morogh.

Fleeing engineers and tinkerers carried whatever prized tools and blueprints they could save. However, the icy mountain passes between Gnomeregan and Coldridge Valley are prowled by indigenous Frostmane trolls. As Felix Whindlebolt scrambled toward the sanctuary of Anvilmar, Frostmane raiders snatched his tool chest, lockbox, and bucket of bolts, carting them off to their camps southwest of town.

Felix Whindlebolt is a gnome engineer who narrowly escaped the radioactive destruction of Gnomeregan. Lacking the martial skill to fight off the dangers of Dun Morogh, he shelters near Anvilmar while attempting to recover his stolen equipment.
felix whindlebolt | who is felix | felix anvilmar

During an unexpected trogg invasion, gnome authorities unleashed volatile radioactive gas intended to wipe out the monsters. The gas contaminated the city's ventilation systems instead, slaughtering or mutating most residents and rendering the capital uninhabitable.
what happened to gnomeregan | gnomeregan radiation | fall of gnomeregan

Frostmane trolls took his chest, box, and bucket of bolts. These native trolls ambush travelers along the mountain trails of Dun Morogh and haul stolen scrap and gear back to their crude encampments southwest of Anvilmar.
who stole the bolts | who has felix's stuff | frostmane trolls
Where did the displaced gnomes seek refuge?
Many gnomes fled across Dun Morogh to the dwarven kingdom of Ironforge, while others sought temporary shelter in smaller settlements like Anvilmar and Kharanos throughout Dun Morogh.
where are gnomes living | gnome refugees | gnome settlement
Why does a bucket of bolts matter so much?

For an exiled gnome tinkerer, tools, specialized screws, and machined bolts represent their entire livelihood. Without proper equipment, refugee engineers have no way to ply their trade, fashion defenses, or rebuild their lives in exile.
why bolts | felix bucket of bolts
What threat do the Frostmane trolls pose to Coldridge Valley?

The Frostmane tribe has long inhabited the harsh peaks of Dun Morogh. With the recent trogg outbreaks and the chaos of the Gnomeregan evacuation, the trolls have grown bolder, raiding supply lines and ambushing travelers.
trolls in dun morogh | frostmane threat | frostmane camp
anvilmar | bucket of bolts | coldridge | felix whindlebolt | frostmane | gnomeregan | radiation
No self-respecting craftsman can stand by while scavengers make off with precision bolts, calipers, and toolboxes that took a lifetime to assemble.
The Coldridge mountains have sheltered your kin for centuries; helping gnome refugees secure their footing in Anvilmar honors the ancient alliance between Ironforge and Gnomeregan.
This quest encapsulates the bitter tragedy facing your people: having lost your wondrous home to poison and betrayal, everyday tinkerers must now beg strangers to pry basic tools from crude trolls.
Why does Felix Whindlebolt want his belongings back?

Having fled the radiation poisoning Gnomeregan with barely the clothes on his back, Felix lost the last remnants of his livelihood and trade. Without his personal chest, box, and tools, he is completely stranded in Anvilmar with no means to rebuild his life or ply his craft as a refugee.
felix motive | why does felix need this | felix whindlebolt belongings
Why can't Felix retrieve his belongings himself?

Felix is an ordinary tinkerer and displaced refugee, not an adventurer or soldier. Terrified by the hostile wilderness and outmatched by the Frostmane trolls who carried off his gear, he cannot risk venturing into their encampments alone.
why doesn't felix get his stuff | why does felix need me | felix why me
What is inside Felix's Box and Chest?

Felix's chest and box contain the personal belongings and specialized tools he managed to pack when fleeing the disaster in Gnomeregan. To a displaced craftsman far from home, these containers hold everything required to make a fresh start.
felix's box | felix's chest | what is in felix's chest
Tran'rek in Gadgetzan wants to get into Thistleshrub Valley, but the strange beasts there keep them away. Clear some of the thistleshrubs out, and Tran'rek might think about going back.

Thistleshrub Valley lies south-west of Gadgetzan, and Tran'rek calls it a mighty dangerous place. They do not trust the strange beasts there, gnarled thistleshrubs and thistleshrub rootshapers, and with so many around they will not go back.

Tran'rek wants eight gnarled thistleshrubs and eight thistleshrub rootshapers cleared out. There is one condition: Tran'rek wants a closer look at the cactus in the valley, so some of it must be left in one piece.

Scalding Mornbrew Delivery is a hurried errand through Coldridge Valley to deliver fresh hot drink before it chills in the mountain frost. Nori Pridedrift entrusts the delivery to an adventurer to ensure Durnan Furcutter receives his mornbrew piping hot.

Dun Morogh's biting cold has ruined many a hot meal, and Mornbrew is no exception. After completing a delivery to Grelin Whitebeard, Nori Pridedrift realizes he lacks the time to bring another fresh cup to Anvilmar before it freezes into an unpalatable slush. Rather than let his customer down, he enlists any swift traveler willing to brave the snow.
The Price of a Warm Mug

Durnan Furcutter, stationed inside the warmth of Anvilmar's mountain hall, is known to be particular about his refreshments. Chilly Mornbrew simply will not do. Delivering the piping drink intact earns a weary dwarf a much-needed break from his duties, though Nori still expects his favorite mug returned in one piece.
Durnan Furcutter is a dwarf residing inside the subterranean hall of Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. He relies on local deliveries from Nori Pridedrift for his hot mornbrew.
durnan furcutter | who is durnan | furcutter
Why does the delivery need to be so fast?
The freezing alpine weather of Coldridge Valley causes hot drinks to cool rapidly. Durnan specifically ordered scalding mornbrew, and cold ale or tea is considered ruined by dwarf standards.
why timed | mornbrew timer | why hurry

Nori Pridedrift is a dwarf stationed out in the snowy paths of Coldridge Valley. He tends to deliveries between local encampments, including bringing drinks to Grelin Whitebeard and workers in Anvilmar.
nori pridedrift | nori | who is nori
Mornbrew is a warm, invigorating dwarven morning brew, crafted to cut through the freezing chill of the Dun Morogh peaks and sustain hardy mountain workers.
Anvilmar is situated directly northeast of Nori's post, carved into the mountain rock of Coldridge Valley to shelter young mountaineers and craftsmen from the blizzards.
where is anvilmar | anvilmar location | find anvilmar
Does Nori want the mug back?
Yes. Once Durnan finishes enjoying his hot brew, he hands back the empty container so it can be returned to Nori in Coldridge Valley.
mug return | bring back the mug | nori's mug
anvilmar | coldridge valley | dun morogh | durnan furcutter | mornbrew | nori pridedrift
Serving beverages at the proper temperature is a mark of true culinary respect, especially under Dun Morogh's punishing sub-zero conditions.
Every dwarf understands the tragedy of cold brew in freezing mountain air, making this dash across the valley a matter of pure principle.
Why does Nori Pridedrift want the mornbrew delivered?

Nori was supposed to deliver fresh, piping-hot mornbrew to Durnan Furcutter, but a prior delivery to Grelin Whitebeard held him up. Durnan specifically expects his brew piping hot, not lukewarm or chilly, so Nori is scrambling to get the drink to Anvilmar before it completely cools off.
why deliver mornbrew | nori motive | why does nori need this delivered
Why does Nori ask you to deliver it instead of taking it himself?

Nori has already fallen behind schedule after stopping to serve Grelin Whitebeard. Knowing the brew only stays scalding hot for a few short minutes, he realizes he cannot sprint up the mountain path quickly enough on his own. Spotting you, he relies on your fresh legs to dash to Anvilmar before the drink turns cold.
why does nori need me | why cant nori deliver it | why me nori delivery

After delivering a piping hot draught of Mornbrew across the snowdrifts of Dun Morogh, one final errand remains: returning the empty tankard. Durnan Furcutter sends the runner back across Coldridge Valley to return Nori Pridedrift's prized mug. It is a simple courtesy, but one the brew seller deeply appreciates.

Serving piping hot Mornbrew out in the biting freeze of Dun Morogh is a delicate business. Once Durnan Furcutter has finished warming his bones with the scalding brew, the empty tankard cannot simply be tossed in the snow. Dwarven hospitality runs on mutual respect, and letting good dishware go missing is a sure way to find oneself cut off from future rounds.

Returning to Coldridge Valley completes the delivery run for Nori Pridedrift. As Nori is fond of reminding forgetful couriers, sturdy drinkware does not simply grow on trees—especially not in the subzero crags of the dwarven homeland. Returning the empty vessel in one piece cements an adventurer's reputation as a reliable hand in the local community.
Durnan Furcutter gives you this task immediately after you deliver the freshly brewed Mornbrew to him out in Dun Morogh.
quest giver | who gives bring back the mug | durnan furcutter quest

You return the empty mug to Nori Pridedrift, who wanders Coldridge Valley in Dun Morogh selling his mornbrew.

No. While the initial delivery of the Scalding Mornbrew had a strict timer to keep the drink piping hot, returning the empty mug can be done at your own pace.

Quality mugs and steins are valuable barware in Dun Morogh. As Nori points out, mugs do not grow on trees, and taverns cannot afford to lose drinkware to every passing courier.

Any proper cook or brewer knows that quality service does not end until the dishware is accounted for and returned to the kitchen.
Every dwarf knows that keeping a tavernkeeper's tankard is a quick route to a brawl; returning Nori's mug is basic dwarven manners.
Why does Durnan Furcutter want this done?

Durnan Furcutter just finished enjoying the piping hot scalding mornbrew delivered by Nori in Coldridge Valley to keep the chill away. Returning the empty mug is basic courtesy to Nori Pridedrift, who expects his glassware back rather than letting couriers leave it scattered out in the freezing snow of Dun Morogh.

Dorius Stonetender is badly hurt in Searing Gorge, light-headed, with the world spinning and bleeding inside. He says he must get back to Ironforge and begs for your help to get him there.

Dorius groans that he is badly injured. He feels light-headed, the world is spinning, and he is bleeding internally. His one wish is to get back to Ironforge, and he asks you to help him make the journey.
The road ends just short of Stonewrought Pass. There Dorius is shot and dies, and a letter he was carrying falls to the ground, singed.
Dorius Stonetender is badly injured in Searing Gorge and needs help getting back to Ironforge.

A singed letter that Dorius let fall is written to his brother. It tells of the Suntara stones, which are real and in the hands of the Dark Irons, whose leader Lathoric the Black uses their power to enslave Dorius's excavation team. It is meant for Thorius at the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge, and you are the one to carry it there.

In the letter, Dorius writes to his brother that if it is being read, he is gone. The stones exist, and the Dark Irons hold them. Their leader, Lathoric the Black, uses their power to enslave Dorius's excavation team. The team was taken to the cauldron, and their minds are twisted as they toil by day and by night to finish something called Obsidion. Dorius begs his brother to help them, his final wish, and asks that those who bring the letter be thanked.
Thorius sobs as the letter is brought. Then Thorius dries his face and swears in the name of the Light that Dorius will have his wish.
Dorius wrote it to his brother, as a message to be read after his death.
who wrote the letter | author of singed letter | dorius letter
Curator Thorius can be found in the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge.
where is thorius | curator thorius location | thorius hall of explorers

The letter says Lathoric the Black and the Dark Irons are using the stones to enslave them. They were taken to the cauldron.

What is the enslaved team working on?

In Nightmares is a Horde quest that tasks an adventurer with carrying a disturbing relic, the Nightmare Shard, to Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem atop Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff. Originally recovered as a glowing fragment from the Wailing Caverns, the shard reveals a deeply unsettling corruption seeping into the Emerald Dream.

After examining the strange crystal retrieved from the depths of the Wailing Caverns, Falla Sagewind recognizes that it is made from the pure essence of the Emerald Dream. Yet the vision dwelling inside is dark and chaotic, bearing the hallmark not of peaceful slumber, but of a waking nightmare. Reluctant to speak openly about such alarming omens, she entrusts the shard to you with instructions to seek out Thunder Bluff's most venerated elder druid, Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem.

When presented with the Nightmare Shard on Elder Rise, Hamuul Runetotem's usual composure falters upon peering inside. Confronted with tangible evidence that the Emerald Dream is unraveling into nightmare, the archdruid chooses his words carefully. He firmly counsels discretion, warning that these delicate matters are far beyond the understanding of ordinary travelers, and quietly resolves to investigate the unseen affliction threatening the slumbering realm.

The Nightmare Shard is the glowing shard recovered in the Wailing Caverns, which Falla Sagewind entrusts to you after examining it. Though forged from the pure spiritual essence of the Emerald Dream, it carries a foul, twisted vision indicating that something in the Dream has gone terribly wrong.
what is nightmare shard | glowing shard nightmare | what did falla find

Falla Sagewind is a knowledgeable tauren druid located on the mountainside overlooking the Wailing Caverns in the Barrens. She studies the anomalous phenomena emerging from the corrupted oasis caverns and sends Horde couriers to Hamuul Runetotem when dangerous relics are discovered.
falla sagewind | who gave me this quest | quest giver
Where can I find Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem?
Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem resides on Elder Rise, one of the elevated mesas of Thunder Bluff. He can be found standing within the druidic circle alongside his fellow Cenarion Circle practitioners.
where is hamuul | hamuul runetotem location | elder rise hamuul
Why does Hamuul want to keep the shard a secret?

The Emerald Dream is the sacred sanctuary of nature and the slumbering druids. Tangible evidence that it is being twisted into a nightmare could cause widespread panic among the Cenarion Circle and undermine fragile spiritual restoration efforts across Kalimdor, prompting Hamuul to urge silence.
why keep it quiet | hamuul secret | why does hamuul hide the shard
Does the Alliance have a version of this quest?

Yes. While Horde champions take the Nightmare Shard to Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem in Thunder Bluff, Alliance players who investigate the Wailing Caverns are directed to take their shard across the sea to Darnassus, presenting it to the druid Mathrengyl Bearwalker of the Cenarion Circle.
alliance version | in nightmares alliance | can alliance do this
How does this relate to the Wailing Caverns?

The shard originates within the Wailing Caverns, where the druid Naralex entered a deep trance to channel underground springs into the Barrens. Instead of healing the land, Naralex's slumber twisted into a waking nightmare, mutating the cavern fauna and bleeding into crystal shards like this one.
wailing caverns connection | naralex connection | how does this relate to naralex
elder rise | emerald dream | falla sagewind | glowing shard | hamuul runetotem | in nightmares | nightmare shard | thunder bluff | wailing caverns
For druids, the shard is deeply alarming evidence that the pristine sanctity of the Emerald Dream is compromised, validating the whispers of corruption creeping through Cenarion circles.

Delivering the shard safeguards the spiritual well-being of central Kalimdor, demonstrating that the Horde plays a crucial role in containing the fungal and dream-born corruption spilling from the Barrens.

Returning to Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem emphasizes the growing prominence of tauren druids within the Cenarion Circle as they confront ancient cosmological threats alongside their night elven teachers.
Why does Falla Sagewind want the Nightmare Shard delivered to Hamuul Runetotem?

When Falla Sagewind examines the shard, she recognizes it as pure essence of the Emerald Dream, but tainted by visions of a waking nightmare. Disturbed by what she sees, she realizes the discovery is far too dangerous and significant for her to handle alone. She refuses to speak of it further and insists you carry it immediately to Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem in Thunder Bluff, trusting only one of the highest-ranking and wisest druids of the Cenarion Circle to understand and manage such a dire omen.
why send shard to hamuul | why does falla want this done | falla sagewind motive

Recovered from the blighted soil and monstrous dens of Duskwood, this battered tome bears the official stamp of the Royal Library of Stormwind. Titled 'The History of Stormwind,' it vanished prior to the kingdom's reconstruction following the First War. Returning it restores a lost chronicle to Head Librarian Milton Sheaf and begins an effort to preserve Southern human history.
A Relic of the First War

Discovered among the hostile undead and brutish ogres roaming Duskwood, this mud-caked volume is a rare surviving artifact from the era before Stormwind's destruction. Bearing the kingdom's formal library seal on its opening page, it was checked out decades ago—before the Horde razed the capital—and was presumed lost forever amid the fall of the south.

When brought back to Milton Sheaf in the Royal Library of Stormwind Keep, the book is recognized as an invaluable treasure destined for the rare books archive. Years of exposure in the haunted wilderness have left its pages badly degraded, and the find spurs Sheaf to recover more lost knowledge, looking north to Southshore, the town closest to the ruined kingdom of Alterac and its abandoned libraries.
The book drops from various hostile creatures roaming Duskwood, most commonly the undead haunting the cemeteries and fields or the ogres occupying the southern hills.
where to find old history book | book drop location | duskwood history book
Who do I bring the book to?
You return the volume to Milton Sheaf, the head librarian situated in the Royal Library inside Stormwind Keep.
turn in location | where do i turn this in | milton sheaf location
Why is the book in such poor condition?

The book was checked out prior to the First War and the sack of Stormwind. It survived decades in the wilderness of Duskwood, weathered by dirt, rot, and the hands of wandering scavengers and monsters.
why is it muddy | why damaged
Does returning this book lead to other tasks?
Yes. Milton Sheaf will send you north to Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills to speak with Loremaster Dibbs, who can direct you to books still lying in the Ruins of Alterac.
what comes next | followup quest | book quest chain
Why does Milton Sheaf care so much about this specific tome?

Because the original kingdom was leveled during the First War, few original historical records survived the burning of the city. Recovering genuine pre-war texts helps scholars reconstruct the kingdom's past.
why is the book important | importance of history of stormwind
Can Horde players complete this quest?
No. The book belongs to the Royal Library of Stormwind and can only be turned in to Alliance librarians within Stormwind Keep.
horde version | is this alliance only
an old history book | duskwood | milton sheaf | preserving knowledge | southshore | stormwind keep | stormwind library | the history of stormwind
Scholars of the arcane understand that ancient libraries hold knowledge vulnerable to decay and neglect when left in the wild.
Recovering pre-war texts restores fragments of Stormwind's lost heritage that survived the devastation of the First War.
For humans of the south, reclaiming written records from the wilderness is a vital step in rebuilding the culture shattered by the Old Horde.

Following the discovery of a strange glowing shard, Falla Sagewind recognizes that the artifact contains the pure essence of the Emerald Dream tainted by dark visions. She dispatches an adventurer to Darnassus to deliver the disturbing relic directly to the elder druids of the Cenarion Circle.

The glowing shard recovered from the depths of Wailing Caverns proves far more dangerous than simple crystal. Upon inspecting it, Falla Sagewind identifies it as an embodiment of the Emerald Dream's purest essence. Yet rather than reflecting the verdant harmony of the natural world, the stone twists with unsettling, fearful visions. Shaken by what she sees, Falla refuses to delve deeper herself and insists the shard must be safely transferred to senior leadership within the Cenarion Circle.

In Darnassus, the relic is presented to Mathrengyl Bearwalker, an experienced druid within the Cenarion Enclave. Greeted initially with calm curiosity, Mathrengyl is visibly unsettled the moment he gazes into the shard's core. Realizing that the corruption plaguing the Barrens connects directly to disturbances deep within the Emerald Dream itself, he quickly hushes further discussion. The elder druid warns that such terrifying anomalies are not matters for common ears, quietly taking custody of the Nightmare Shard to study the encroaching shadow.

The Nightmare Shard is a crystallized piece of the Emerald Dream's essence, originally recovered as a mysterious glowing shard. Instead of reflecting natural harmony, it emanates dark visions and corrupting power, revealing that a sinister presence has begun invading the Dream.
what is nightmare shard | glowing shard lore | emerald dream shard

Falla Sagewind is a tauren druid of nature's lore who inspects strange relics found across the wilds. Upon realizing the true, terrifying origin of the glowing shard, she refers travelers to higher druidic authorities in Darnassus.

Mathrengyl Bearwalker is an elder druid trainer of the Cenarion Circle stationed at the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus. He acts as an experienced mentor and investigates serious spiritual threats affecting nature and the Emerald Dream.
mathrengyl bearwalker | bearwalker darnassus | who is mathrengyl
Why is Mathrengyl so secretive about the shard?

The Emerald Dream is revered as the pristine, inviolable realm of nature guided by the Green Dragonflight and the sleeping druids. Evidence that this realm is suffering from nightmarish corruption represents a profound spiritual crisis, one the Cenarion Circle is reluctant to expose to the public.
why secret | what does mathrengyl hide | why won't mathrengyl talk
Where does this quest chain begin?

The storyline begins with 'The Glowing Shard', an item found on Mutanus the Devourer at the culmination of the Wailing Caverns. That shard is brought to scholars who eventually trace its ominous origins toward Darnassus or Thunder Bluff.
in nightmares prereq | where did this start | how to get in nightmares
Do Horde players have an equivalent quest?

Yes. While Alliance heroes report to Mathrengyl Bearwalker in Darnassus, Horde champions deliver their findings to Hamuul Runetotem on the Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff, discovering the same unsettling news about the Emerald Dream.
horde version | is there a horde in nightmares | in nightmares horde
cenarion circle | cenarion enclave | darnassus | emerald dream | falla sagewind | glowing shard | in nightmares | mathrengyl bearwalker | nightmare shard
For druids, this quest reveals that the sacred Emerald Dream is not the untouched sanctuary they were taught to commune with, hinting at profound internal danger.
Alliance adventurers carrying this relic into the heart of Darnassus offer the night elf leadership an early glimpse of the corruption spreading beneath the world's surface.
Night elves venerate the slumbering realm where Malfurion Stormrage resides; discovering a waking nightmare inside its essence strikes at the core of their spiritual heritage.
Why does Falla Sagewind want the Nightmare Shard delivered?

Falla Sagewind recognized that the shard contains the essence of the Emerald Dream, but the vision she glimpsed within was deeply twisted into a nightmare. Alarmed by what she saw and knowing such ominous corruption lies far beyond her understanding, she insists that it be examined by a wise druid of the Cenarion Circle in Darnassus immediately.

A dying archaeologist in Searing Gorge urges you to release those whom the power of the Suntara still drives to keep at their labor, though their bodies have given out. Everything hinges on the altar of Suntara, and a relic guarded by Twilight's Hammer must be placed upon it.

Before collapsing, the archaeologist begs you to release them. Their bodies have given out, yet the Suntara's power drives them on to keep at their labor. The key, says the archaeologist, is the altar of Suntara.

Go northwest, to the hills above the cave. Idolaters of the Twilight's Hammer guard a relic there, called the Mysterious Artifact. Take it from them and bring it to the Slag Pit, to set upon the altar of Suntara.

You engage the Oathstone of Ysera's Dragonflight, and Itharius speaks straight into your mind. Taking up the charge means helping Ysera's Dragonflight redeem the corrupted soul of Eranikus, and the first sacrifice is to give Itharius the gem that chains the part of Eranikus' mind that is still free. Itharius waits in the Swamp of Sorrows.

Through the Oathstone, Itharius tells you that accepting this charge means aiding Ysera's Dragonflight to redeem the corrupted soul of Eranikus. Itharius expects many sacrifices from the two of you, and the first is to hand over the gem that has bound whatever free-willed part of Eranikus' mind remains. The Oathstone and the Chained Essence of Eranikus must go to Itharius in the Swamp of Sorrows, and there you choose whether to aid the dragonflight.

Itharius greets you at yet another crossroads and asks what choice you make. Once it is made, Itharius says your choices so far have been the correct ones, and that your actions from here on will decide whether that continues.
Itharius speaks into your mind through the Oathstone for Ysera's Dragonflight, and waits in the Swamp of Sorrows, seeking to redeem the corrupted soul of Eranikus.

Break Sharptusk! is a decisive rite of passage issued by Brave Windfeather on Red Cloud Mesa. To secure the tauren homeland against ongoing raids, young champions are sent east into Brambleblade Ravine to slay Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle. Eliminating the Bristleback chieftain strikes a severe blow against the quilboar encroaching upon Mulgore.

The grassy heights of Red Cloud Mesa have long served as a peaceful sanctuary where young tauren learn the traditions of the hunt and attunement with the Earth Mother.
